title: VPC landing framework: matrix & operator checklist (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note is a lightweight operator-focused landing framework for customer VPC/on-prem onboarding. It is intended to sit between high-level reference architectures and the day-to-day runbooks we hand to SRE/solutions engineers during a customer ramp. The goal: provide a compact matrix to pick patterns, an explicit Terraform module compatibility checklist, and a runbook-style operator checklist for staging -> production cutovers and upgrades.

Why this exists (context):
- We frequently see repeated questions when onboarding regulated customers: IP planning, NAT/egress model, private endpoints, DNS delegation, and drift between customer-provided templates and our TF modules.
- Current playbooks are fragmented (design notes, TF snippets, cutover lists). This doc collects pragmatic choices, common gotchas, and an operator-ready sequence for customer ramps.

Audience:
- Solutions Engineering (customer-facing design and handoff)
- Private Deployments Operators (SREs doing the provisioning and cutover)
- Terraform module maintainers (compat/upgrade checklist)

Top-level matrix (pick one row per customer):
- Customer profile: "Greenfield cloud tenant" -> Connectivity pattern: Transit Gateway / VPC-peering allowed -> NAT: Centralized egress via TGW -> TF module set: vpc-core v2, tgw-attachment v1 -> Accepts automated route propagation: yes -> Typical IP blocks: 10.0.0.0/16 for tenant VPC, 10.10.0.0/16 for Redwood-managed pool.
- Customer profile: "Strict air-gapped" -> Connectivity pattern: Direct cross-connect or on-prem physical circuit -> NAT: Customer-managed NAT appliances -> TF module set: onprem-bootstrap v0.9 + custom carrier docs -> Accepts automated scripts: no -> IPs: per customer provided RFC1918 blocks.
- Customer profile: "Shared services + multiple tenants" -> Connectivity pattern: Transit hub + segmented tenant VPCs -> NAT: Egress via shared services VPC with NAT gateway or egress appliances -> TF module set: hub-and-spoke v1, subnet-slicing helper -> Accepts automated rollouts: partial

Decision checklist (for solutions eng before provisioning):
- Confirm CIDR ownership and future growth plan (get at least 2x expected host count headroom).
- Determine egress model: customer NAT vs Redwood-managed NAT (impacts logs and IP allowlist).
- Confirm whether DNS delegation is allowed (if not, we must use private endpoints + customer route53 endpoints or static IPs).
- Confirm KMS/HSM key custody requirements (bring-your-own-key vs Redwood KMS integration).
- Confirm compliance constraints for routing logs, flow logs retention, and audit log export destination.
- Confirm ACLs/Firewall appliance placement and whether we will run health probes across those appliances.

Terraform module compatibility checklist (operators + module owners):
- Module versions pinned: ensure all modules referenced by the onboarding plan are pinned in the deployment repo (no floating tags).
- Provider lockfile present: run terraform init -upgrade locally and check that the lockfile is committed.
- State isolation: every customer must have their own state backend and locking (S3 bucket + DynamoDB or equivalent).
- Variable surface area: reduce required variables in the module to a short list for operator runbooks. Use defaults for nonessential knobs.
- Upgrade plan: Add a migration path doc with exact terraform plan output for minor and major version upgrades.
- Idempotency checks: run terraform plan twice after a successful apply; the second plan should show zero changes. Document exceptions and acceptable transient diffs (e.g., AWS-assigned IDs).

Operator provisioning runbook (staging cut - checklist):
1) Preflight (day 0):
  - Validate customer CIDRs and add to shared denylist for collision detection.
  - Validate IAM roles: operator service account, customer cross-account read roles, and any assumed roles used by the modules.
  - Confirm secrets: KMS key ARNs, any certs to be imported, and whether HSM integration will be used.
  - Create per-customer S3 state bucket name and DynamoDB lock table; apply least-privilege policies.
  - Run terraform validate against the deployed module versions.
2) Provision (day 1):
  - Apply core VPC module in staging tenant environment. Capture outputs: vpc_id, public_subnets, private_subnets, route_table_ids.
  - Provision peering / TGW attachments in staging. Wait for status "available" and route propagation.
  - Configure NSGs/firewalls and run connectivity smoke tests (ping to bastion, curl health endpoints).
  - Stand up private endpoints for the Redwood control plane (if customer allows).
3) Pre-cut checks (day 2):
  - Run automated acceptance tests (see preflight script list below).
  - Validate logs: flow logs, guardrails, and Alertmanager hooks.
  - Security scan: run terraform-compliance ruleset for known anti-patterns.
4) Production cut (day 3):
  - Repeat apply with production variables (scale, subnet sizing).
  - Perform incremental DNS delegation/route changes during maintenance window.
  - Monitor metrics intensively for first 2 hours: packet loss, RTOs, API timeouts, and egress rate limits.
5) Post-cut (day 4+):
  - Run daily drift detection for 7 days.
  - Lock down IAM paths used only during onboarding.
  - Export acceptance artifacts to the customer: IP lists, subnet maps, and terraform state access instructions.

Preflight smoke & acceptance scripts (examples to wire into CI):
- Network reachability: probe from Redwood bastion to private endpoints and customer-provided app endpoints on configured ports.
- DNS validation: ensure private hosted zone resolution from within tenant VPC.
- Egress validation: outbound IPs match expected NAT pool.
- KV cache / latency probes for inference testpoints (small prompt roundtrips) if control-plane endpoints are in customer network.
- Failover test: simulate AZ-loss by temporarily disabling an AZ's subnet route in staging and verify service fallback.

Rollback and emergency tactics:
- Quick rollback: re-apply last-known-good terraform state from the state bucket snapshot. Keep snapshots hourly during cut.
- Network rollback: revert route propagation and peering attachments first (these are the highest blast radius).
- If NAT/egress change caused issues: re-route via backup egress (we recommend keeping a minimal redundant egress path as an emergency measure).
- Communication: precreate templated status messages for customers and internal channels with the exact out-of-band IPs and steps.

Common pitfalls and mitigations (lessons learned):
- Pitfall: customer CIDR overlaps our Redwood-managed pools. Mitigation: maintain a CIDR registry and require customers to run the overlap checker before handoff.
- Pitfall: asymmetric routing when appliances are introduced mid-cut. Mitigation: ensure stateful path tests and that firewalls permit return traffic from all expected subnets.
- Pitfall: TF modules drift because of manually applied customer changes. Mitigation: enforce a change window, record manual exceptions in the customer "operator exceptions" doc, and schedule reconciliation tasks.

Operational metrics to monitor during and after onboarding (SLO-focused):
- Control-plane: API success rate (target 99.9%), median API latency, 95th/99th percentile latency.
- Network: packet loss rate, retransmit rate, egress throughput per customer, NAT connection saturation.
- Security/observability: flow log delivery error rate, audit log ingestion latency, number of unauthorized access attempts.

Notes for module maintainers (compatibility hints):
- Keep AMI/instance profiles out of top-level modules; expose a small variable to select instance class and map to AMIs in a separate config file.
- Document all resources that create ephemeral IDs (ENIs, route table associations) so operators know which diffs are expected.
- Provide a migration script for modules that rename outputs or change output shapes (emit a compatibility shim in the next minor release).

Appendix A: example minimal variables file (operator copy-paste)
- customer_name = "acme-inc"
- region = "us-west-2"
- vpc_cidr = "10.240.0.0/16"
- public_subnet_cidrs = ["10.240.0.0/20", "10.240.16.0/20"]
- private_subnet_cidrs = ["10.240.32.0/20", "10.240.48.0/20"]
- enable_flow_logs = true
- egress_model = "centralized-tgw"

Appendix B: quick troubleshooting recipes
- No DNS resolution in VPC: confirm route53 resolver rules are associated with the VPC and VPC endpoints in place; check security group egress for DNS port 53.
- Flow logs not appearing: ensure S3/GCL sink permissions and that the flow logs resource is in the plan; check delivery failure metrics.
- Peering shows pending: verify both sides created peering and that accept step executed; check for overlapping CIDRs.

Open questions / follow-ups (to capture in huddle):
- Should we add a small standardized egress bastion that can be used as an emergency NAT path for all customers? Pros/cons and cost analysis required.
- Do we want an optional module that creates a minimal customer-side observability stack (Prometheus node-exporter + log forwarder) to standardize metrics?
- What audit retention period defaults should we bake into modules for enterprise customers?

Next actions (owner: Sanjay):
- Convert the above matrix into a short decision-tree flowchart and add to the public onboarding template. (due: 2025-03-10)
- Add CI tests that run the idempotency check for the core VPC module on PRs. (due: 2025-03-05)
- Review the emergency egress proposal with platform-sre. (due: 2025-03-12)

Revision history:
- 2025-02-12 initial draft
- 2025-02-20 added TF compatibility checklist and operator runbook steps
- 2025-03-01 clarified rollback steps and added preflight script list

End of document.
